title: Monitoring the Wall Mechanics During Stent Deployment in a Vessel
protocol: Fix both ends of the latex vessel to barbed hose connections fastened on a sturdy workbench.
Measure the area of interest on the latex vessel to determine the field of view.
Record the distance from the outside edge of one barbed hose connector to the center location between the connectors.
Translate this distance onto the catheter by measuring from the center of the stent up the catheter.
Mark the catheter with a marker at the translated distance.
Remove the latex vessel from the barbed hose connectors.
Prepare the latex vessel by spraying the area of interest with a stochastic pattern of white and black spray paint or marking it with random dots using permanent marker.
Select the calibration panel that is slightly larger than the area of interest measured in step 1.
Place the calibration panel between the barbed hose connectors at the area of interest.
Ensure that the area of interest is well lit.
Adjust the distance between two cameras based on the selected calibration panel.
Adjust the distance from the sample based on the selected calibration panel.
Adjust the camera height based on the selected calibration panel.
Open a new project in ARAMIS by selecting "File", then "New Project".
Click on the "Sensor" tab and select "Calibration", then "Full Calibration".
With the lens aperture fully open, focus the camera on the calibration panel.
Loosen the set screw on the camera and rotate the lens to focus.
Retighten the set screw after focusing.
Close the lens aperture.
Take the first image of the calibration process.
Displace or rotate the calibration panel according to the demonstration on the computer.
Focus the camera until the image is clear on the computer screen.
Take the second image.
Repeat this process for the remainder of the calibration images.
Once all calibration images are taken, calculate the calibration settings in ARAMIS.
Re-calibrate if the calibration deviation is greater than 0.04.
Remove the calibration panel and place the painted latex vessel back onto the barbed hose connectors.
Determine the number of frames per second for the test.
Adjust the shutter speed to less than 1 frame per second and ensure no red is displayed on the image.
Take 5 images.
Add start points on the image series and compute the test.
While holding "ctrl", click on the center of the sample to observe background noise.
If pretest noise is above 75 microstrain, redo the calibration process.
Select the amount of images desired for the stent expansion test.
Gradually insert the catheter into the latex vessel using the marker indicator.
Insert the stent until it reaches the central location in the vessel.
Begin taking images with ARAMIS during stent insertion and deployment.
For balloon-expandable stents, gradually increase the balloon pressure to expand the stent fully.
After full expansion, gradually decrease the pressure of the balloon to zero and withdraw the balloon and catheter.
For self-expanding stents, gradually remove the sheath until the stent is fully expanded.
Gradually retract the catheter after full stent expansion for self-expanding stents.
Create a stage point by holding "ctrl" and clicking on the area of interest for strain analysis.
Select the type of strain desired for analysis.
Create a multistage point line by clicking on the "sections" tab, then "create section".
Select a line on the image parallel to the X axis at Y equals zero.
In the upper tool bar select "primitives", then "best fit cylinder".
Select a small section of the image using the "select through surface" tool on the right tool bar.
Under the "analysis" tab click on "point to point distance".
Select two points on the image for analysis.
